advances: The parity disjointness is for selected atomic witnesses. The outside-mass conclusion is conditional on strict quotas.

proof:
For an integer base $r\in P\cap\operatorname{conv}J$, form a deepest mark at $r$ from deepest marks over the chosen inputs in $J$. A closed base halfspace containing $r$ contains some input base of positive weight. The depth at each of the finitely many chosen input bases is strictly greater than $Q$, so their minimum is strictly greater than $Q$, and hence so is $b_{\rm base}(r)$. Thus $r\in J$. If instead $r\in P\cap\operatorname{conv}A$, forming a deepest mark again yields $r\in I$. Heredity excludes $r\in J$ because every input of positive weight belongs to $A$. This proves completeness of both sets.

For nonempty $A$, apply efc6257ea1f83bc1 to its midpoint-closed set of sites of common atomic depth $Q\in(0,M)$, using all weights on $P$. Its $m$ caps have exact mass $Q$ and their exclusive boundary witnesses have distinct parities by that lemma's proof. No cap contains any $t\in J$, since its mass is below $b_{\rm base}(t)$. If one witness $p_i$ shared a parity with such a $t$, their midpoint would be integer in $I$ by completeness. In every retained cap's defining inequality, $p_i$ is at equality in its own cap and strictly excluded in the others, and $t$ is strictly excluded everywhere. The midpoint is therefore strictly outside all caps. Since the caps cover $A$, it belongs to $J$, contradicting heredity with the atomic input $p_i$. This proves disjointness and the parity count, including the empty case.

When both strata are nonempty, $V_A\le mQ$ by the cover and $V_J<k(J)M/k(P)$ by the quota for the proper closed minor $J$. Subtracting from $M$ gives the strict bound. If $I=P$, $A\ne\varnothing$ and $Q/M<1/k(P)$, that bound has positive right side when $J\ne\varnothing$, by $m+k(J)\le k(P)$. This contradicts $V_{P\setminus I}=0$. If $J=\varnothing$, the cover and $m\le k(P)$ instead give $M\le mQ<M$.

statement:
Use the positive buffered mixed setting and $P,M,Q,I,J,A$ of proper buffered deepest-input heredity, and let $k(T)$ count the occupied parities of $T$ in the inherited affine lattice, with $k(\varnothing)=0$. Both $J=P\cap\operatorname{conv}J$ and $A=P\cap\operatorname{conv}A$. There are $m$ closed pure-base halfspaces of raw weighted mass $Q$ covering $A$ and excluding $J$, each with an exclusive boundary witness in $A$. Their witness parities are distinct and disjoint from the parities of $J$, so $m+k(J)\le k(I)$. Take $m=0$ if $A$ is empty.

Write $V_T=\sum_{z\in T}|K_z|$ and suppose every nonempty proper closed minor $T=P\cap\operatorname{conv}T$ satisfies $V_T<k(T)M/k(P)$. If $A$ and $J$ are nonempty, then $V_{P\setminus I}>M[1-k(J)/k(P)-mQ/M]$. Under the quotas, $I=P$ and $Q/M<1/k(P)$ imply $A=\varnothing$.
title: Exact atomic cap budgets with parities disjoint from proper deepest bases
